title: improv·artist · collage (Wangechi Mutu)
mutation_directive: improv artist: collage via Wangechi Mutu

improv_extras.practice: ink and collage hybrids; mythic figures, Afrofuturist body

v1.feedback: The differential growth ring rising vertically is a solid structural idea for a torso/spine, but the three particle layers read as concentric halos around a tube rather than a mythic hybrid figure — there's no limb articulation, no asymmetry, no collage-like discontinuity that would evoke Mutu's cut-and-reassemble aesthetic. The aura layer is essentially a cylindrical curl-noise cloud, which is exactly the ambient nebula failure mode the brief penalizes. To actually land 'collage body,' break the radial symmetry: graft distinct growth systems at different heights (a branching coral shoulder, a vascular arm tendril, an insect-wing fan) so the silhouette reads as assembled from incompatible anatomies rather than a single homogeneous column. The palette is tasteful but monotone — Mutu's work juxtaposes warm skin tones against cool botanical greens and deep reds, so introduce at least one contrasting hue band tied to a specific anatomical zone.

v2.feedback: The zone-mapped body plan genuinely reads as collage — five distinct differential-growth patches with separate palettes and growth parameters composing a mythic figure is a legitimate translation of Mutu's layered-body practice. Two things to sharpen: the additive blending will wash out zone boundaries where curves overlap (torso meets shoulder, arm meets torso), losing the hard-edge material juxtaposition that makes collage feel like collage — consider alpha blending or a slight gap/dark seam between zones. Second, the crown and shoulder curves grow on the XZ plane and get tilted into place, but their silhouettes will read as generic radial blobs from the default camera; give them anisotropic pressure or directional bias so they fan upward like Mutu's horn/headdress motifs rather than expanding symmetrically.
